agent.problem: The blank asks for the unseen wording “tribes and clans.” Nothing in cards 1–3 gives the baker a basis for reasoning out “clans,” so this becomes a guess at the next word of the line rather than a test of meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Too many choices depend on discovering a fact rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 2, 6, 10, 14, 16 and 18 provide no earlier-card basis for working out the Exodus reminder, Benjamin, Saul's height, the writing of the scroll, Saul's companions or Saul's silence. That makes six of the ten choice cards discovery questions, so most choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
